items.title: Leslie Gourse interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 9, 1996
items.q: I think with the biographies of Billie and Aretha and Mahalia, I was told what to do because I would not have picked Mahalia or Aretha, because they’re not jazz people.

ctx.x: Now do the publishers request that you write these? How does that work? I mean you seem to have quite a good resume here.

Well I did do a little proposal for a book on Monk, and just in conversation with the Schirmer Books editor, someone told me to call, he needed some anthologies. So I did. And he asked me what I did, he said, “What are you working on now?” And I said well I’m doing this and that. And he said, “Gee I’d like you to do a biography for us sometime.” I said, “Well, I have a couple of proposals.” One was on Carmen McRae and one was on Monk and one was on Ella. And he said, “Oh, I’d like the one on Monk, you can send…
You have some nice quotes about — returning to Joe for a moment — did you find him an easy interview? © Fillius Jazz Archive -6-
